title: Cellular systems and 5G
subtitle: Reusing the same radio frequencies in neighbouring cells is what makes mobile phones scale.

cell.title: The cellular idea
cell.body: Radio spectrum is scarce. Instead of one powerful transmitter for a city, divide the area into cells, each with a low-power base station. Cells far enough apart can reuse the same frequencies. A cluster of N cells uses all the available channels once; with N cells per cluster each cell gets 1/N of the total. Hexagons are the usual picture because they tile the plane.
cell.steps: A system has 120 channels and a cluster size N = 4. Each cell gets 120 / 4 = 30 channels; a city of 100 cells then supports 3000 simultaneous calls instead of 120.

interf.title: Interference and handoff
interf.body: Co-channel interference comes from cells reusing your frequency; adjacent-channel interference from neighbouring frequencies. As a moving phone leaves a cell the network performs a handoff to the next cell without dropping the call: the signal strength from the old station falls below a threshold while the new one rises. Hard handoff breaks before making; soft handoff (CDMA) connects to both for a moment.

gens.title: From 1G to 5G
gens.body: 1G: analog voice (AMPS). 2G: digital voice and SMS (GSM, TDMA; GPRS brought packet data). 3G: CDMA-based, mobile internet (UMTS). 4G (LTE): all-IP, OFDMA, tens to hundreds of Mb/s. 5G: higher speeds, very low latency (~1 ms), massive device counts, using sub-6 GHz and millimetre-wave bands and network slicing. GSM architecture: mobile station, base transceiver station, base station controller, mobile switching centre with home/visitor registers.

five.title: 5G, SDN, IoT and the cloud
five.body: 5G’s three use cases: enhanced mobile broadband, ultra-reliable low-latency communication (remote surgery, vehicles) and massive machine-type communication (IoT sensors). Software-defined networking and network function virtualisation run core functions as software in the cloud; edge computing puts processing near the user to cut latency.

prac.title: Numericals
prac.steps: The reuse distance D relates to cell radius R and cluster size N by D = R√(3N). For N = 7 and R = 2 km.

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• Reuse frequencies across clusters; handoff keeps calls alive.
  • Generations: analog → digital → CDMA → all-IP → low latency + massive IoT.
